texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 10.03.2021 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the facts of the case, on 26.08.2020 at about 06.45 Pm , Pankaj Negi along with his friend Arvind Kumar were going from the side of Meethapur Chowk to Kalindi Kunj on Canal Road on the motorcycle bearing no. DL 3SDC 5765 belonging to Arvind Kumar, which Pankaj was driving and Arvind Kumar was sitting as pillion rider, to buy medicine in a normal speed by obeying the traffic rules and regulations. When they reached near Meethapur chowk, Agra Canal Road, towards Kalindi Kunj, Delhi, all of a sudden the offending vehicle bearing no. DL 1LQ 8996, which was driven by its driver in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle with great force and due to the forceful impact, he and his friend along with motorcycle fell down on the road and he received grievous injury. Page No. 2 of 30 :3: Champion was apprehended on the spot by Arvind along with public person gathered there. 3. Further such Arvind and Pankaj Negi were taken to Apollo Hospital, New Delhi and their MLC were prepared. They were discharged from the said hospital later on. 4. Arvind again took treatment from Holy Family Hospital in the OPD, after discharge from the Apollo Hospital. 5. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 337, 338, IPC, & 3, 181, 5, 180 MV Act filed against the R-1 apart from filing of present DAR. As per the claim of IO, accused / R-1 was driving such offending vehicle without any driving license. It is further stated that he was found in drunken state at the time of accident. 6. As per record, R-1/ driver & 2 / owner appeared initially and thereafter stopped appearing. Further they did not file any reply. 7. But, reply/ response filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, in such reply, it is stated that as per the investigation of IO and charge sheet filed, driver / R-1 was not holding driving license at the time of accident and as such. Insurance Company is not liable to pay any such compensation accordingly. It is further Arvind Kumar vs . Sanjay Singh Rawat & Ors. on 7 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181864506/ 2 submitted that in case, R-1 & 2 failed to contest, then R-3 be given leave to take all defences, as per law. It is further stated that there is a contributory negligence on the part of petitioner/ claimant himself. 8. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal as far as present petitioner is concerned: MACT No.: 265/21 Arvid Kumar Vs. Sanjay Singh Rawat & Ors. Page No. 3 of 30 :4: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 26.08.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL1LQ 8996 being driven by R1 & owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP. 2. 3. Relief. 9. As per record, injured examined himself only as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 10. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 11. As per record, insurance company also led evidence. Such insurance company examined Ms. Mehak Aggarwal, R3W1 as the only respondent side witness. She relied upon various documents as Ex.R3W1/1 to Ex.R3W1/6. She was not cross examined by Ld. Counsel for petitioner or R-1 & 2. 12. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.
